## Evidence

The repository ships a validator for tracker data quality and never runs it on its own tracker. Grepping every workflow for pm self-checks returns exactly two hits, both `changelog:pm:check` (`ci.yml:200`, `release.yml:108`). No workflow invokes `pm validate` or `pm health`. `release:gates` covers source quality — eslint suppressions, coverage pragmas, docstring coverage, package boundary, token budget, SDK surface snapshot, entrypoint costs, transport floor — and stops at the source tree.

Consequence, measured 2026-07-25 on this workspace (2,022 items):

| warning | count | declared owner |
|---|---|---|
| validate_resolution_missing_fields | 287 | pm-wenq |
| validate_files_missing_linked_paths | 173 | pm-j8z6 |
| validate_metadata_missing_close_reason | 18 | pm-e9zh |
| validate_metadata_duplicate_issue_codes | 1 | pm-pivf |
| validate_metadata_missing_acceptance_criteria | 1 | *(none — new drift)* |
| validate_metadata_missing_estimate | 1 | *(none — new drift)* |

The last two rows are the argument. Both pointed at a single item created earlier the same day by another agent harness, filed without acceptance criteria and without an estimate. Nothing in CI noticed. It was found by a human-initiated review pass and repaired by hand, which is precisely the control this repository refuses to accept for source code and currently accepts for tracker data.

The first four rows are the other half of the argument: each is a long-lived legacy population with a named owner, and each has drifted upward at times (the resolution faucet is documented as having leaked and been hand-backfilled at least three times, and the files baseline moved 161 to 168 to 173 across three measurements). Owners exist; enforcement does not, so the only thing standing between the tracker and unbounded drift is whether a review pass happens to run.

## Deliverable

A committed baseline of per-warning counts and a gate that fails CI when any count exceeds its baseline, in the shape this repository already uses successfully for eslint suppressions, coverage pragmas, and the SDK import boundary.

- The baseline is shrinking-only: a count may go down and the baseline is ratcheted down with it; it may never go up.
- Each baseline entry names its owning item, so a failure tells an agent which item to read rather than only which check tripped. Warning classes with no owner fail closed — an unowned warning is a filing gap, not an acceptable state.
- The gate runs against the repository's own `.agents/pm`, using the installed build, and is fast enough for the pull-request path rather than nightly only (`pm validate --json` over 2,022 items is well inside the existing gate budget).
- `pm health` is included on the same footing. Its `ok:false` state has previously been reported as an outstanding condition with no gate consuming it, so a health regression is invisible in CI by construction today.
- New warning classes appearing in the validator are a gate failure until the baseline is updated deliberately, which is what keeps the ratchet honest when the validator itself grows checks.

## Relationship to neighbours

- pm-wenq is the mutation-time half: it stops new close-time debt at the moment of closing. This is the CI half: it stops every other kind of drift, including drift introduced by agents whose harness does not run local validation. Both are needed and neither substitutes for the other.
- pm-k6t4yb registers gates and demands a negative-control fixture for each; this gate is one of its subjects and should ship with the known-bad fixture that proves it fails.
- pm-rtn5h6 turns escaped defects into gates; this is the same ratchet shape applied to data rather than code.
- The per-warning owner mapping already exists as maintainer knowledge and has been reconstructed by hand in review after review. Committing it as data is the durable form of that knowledge.
Tracker data-quality ratchet in CI: pm validate and pm health run against this repository's own workspace with a shrinking-only per-warning baseline

CI runs no pm self-check beyond changelog drift, so every tracker data-quality warning class accumulates unenforced and new drift is caught only when a human-initiated review happens to run. Commit a per-warning baseline with owner ids and fail CI when any count regresses, matching the eslint-suppression and import-boundary ratchets already in use for source quality.

A committed baseline file records the current count for every pm validate warning class plus pm health status, with the owning item id for each entry; a CI gate runs pm validate and pm health against the repository's own workspace using the installed build and fails when any count exceeds its baseline or when health regresses; the baseline is shrinking-only, so an improvement ratchets it down and a regression cannot be absorbed by editing the number upward without an explicit reviewed change; a warning class with no declared owner fails the gate, so unowned drift is a filing gap rather than an accepted state; a newly introduced validator check fails the gate until the baseline is deliberately extended; a negative-control fixture proves the gate fails on a known-bad workspace as pm-k6t4yb requires; the gate runs on the pull-request path within the existing gate time budget

value.text:
Re-verified 2026-07-26 and the gap is unchanged: a grep across every workflow finds exactly two tracker-quality invocations, both of them changelog:pm:check (ci.yml:200 and release.yml:110). No workflow runs pm validate or pm health against this repository's own tracker, so the only data-quality property CI defends is that CHANGELOG.md matches what the generator would emit.

Two new invariants were established in this repository today and neither has a gate, which sharpens what this item needs to cover:

1. Every terminal item now carries a release identifier derived from the tag containing its close event — 1,782 of 1,795 stamped, the remaining 13 deliberately unstamped because they close after the newest tag. This is what makes a metadata write on a closed item changelog-neutral. Nothing prevents the next release from closing items without a stamp, at which point attribution silently reverts to updated_at for those items and the drag returns one release at a time rather than all at once, which is harder to notice.

2. Every terminal item that has a parent now carries a typed edge to it, and the terminal corpus carries roughly 3,900 evidence-derived relationship edges. Nothing prevents the next closed item from being terminal with zero typed out-edges, so the graph completeness achieved by a bulk pass decays by attrition.

Both are exactly the shape this item describes — a property that a bulk pass establishes and that only a ratchet keeps. Suggest the gate assert deltas rather than absolutes (no new terminal item without attribution, no new terminal item without a typed edge where a parent exists), so the historical residual lists do not have to be empty for CI to be green.

value.text:
Correction to the preceding comment, and a sharper statement of the gap. My grep matched the literal string "pm validate" and therefore missed the invocations that call the built CLI. CI does run tracker checks, under the static gate in ci.yml:207-216: validate --check-storage-integrity --json, plus history --verify --strict-exit on a single dynamically selected representative item. Those exist for merge safety (pm-iwsj) and the single-stream sampling is the finding pm-pdr8t1 owns.

So the accurate gap is narrower and worth stating precisely: CI runs the storage-integrity check but runs none of the data-quality checks — no default validate profile, no --check-resolution, no --check-history-drift, and no pm health at all. The live counts those would surface today are validate_resolution_missing_fields:289 and health ok:true with telemetry_queue_pending:5. A ratchet is therefore the right shape rather than a pass/fail gate, exactly as this item already specifies: the 289 is a legacy set owned by pm-wenq and must not have to reach zero for CI to be green.

The two new invariants noted above still hold and are still ungated — terminal release attribution and terminal typed-edge coverage — and neither is covered by --check-storage-integrity, which validates artifact parseability rather than field completeness.

value.author: harness:claude-code
value.text: A live defect escape closes the argument for this item, 2026-07-29. CI runs exactly one tracker check, ci.yml line 206, node dist/cli.js validate --check-storage-integrity --check-history-drift --strict-exit, plus changelog:pm:check at line 187 and again in release.yml line 113. Those are integrity and changelog gates. None of the five data-quality checks - metadata, resolution, lifecycle, files, dependency_references - runs anywhere in CI. What escaped: commit c90adb1ea introduced a scalar parent on seven v1 milestone Epics pointing at pm-j7a, which is correct on its own channel but collides with pre-existing inverted child dependency rows on the same seven pairs. The result was validate_hierarchy_parent_cycle with eight named ids and the sample path pm-2xl to pm-j7a to pm-2xl. That commit passed CI Gates, a further feature commit landed on top of it, the 2026.7.29 release was cut from that tree, and the artifact was published to npm - all with a hierarchy cycle in the tracker and every gate green. It was found only because a human-directed session ran pm validate by hand the next morning. The storage-integrity and history-drift checks cannot catch it by construction: the bytes are well formed and every hash verifies; the defect is semantic. That is the exact gap this item names. Two consequences for the acceptance shape. First, the ratchet must cover the lifecycle and metadata checks specifically, because those are the two that detect contradictions rather than corruption. Second, a warning-count ratchet is the right instrument rather than a pass-fail gate, because the corpus carries known legacy classes that cannot go to zero - today 179 stale linked paths and 291 missing resolution fields, both on terminal holders - and a gate that must be green would simply be disabled. The count of warning CLASSES moved 7 to 4 during today's repair; that number is the ratchet.
